result.summary: Resets the request ID and JSON-RPC version fields at the beginning of JSONRPCRequest::parse before validating whether the input payload is an object. This prevents malformed, non-object batch elements from inheriting the ID and version of the preceding element in their error replies.
result.problem: During JSON-RPC batch processing, ExecuteHTTPRPC reuses a single JSONRPCRequest instance across all elements. When an element is not a JSON object, parse() throws an invalid request exception before resetting id and m_json_version, causing the error response to reuse the previous request's ID or be dropped entirely if the preceding call was a JSON-RPC 2.0 notification.
evidence: PR description: 'For [{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2] the reply has two objects with "id":"X", one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped.'
Functional test in test/functional/interface_rpc.py confirms both failure modes on master and verifies that error replies now have null IDs and are not suppressed following notifications.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantive changes to the approach; updated patch ID reflecting a rebase or minor comment adjustment.
result.card: Resets the request ID and JSON-RPC version fields at the start of JSONRPCRequest::parse before verifying whether the input is an object. In JSON-RPC batches, Bitcoin Core reuses a single request instance; non-object elements throw an error before clearing those fields, causing error replies to inherit the prior element's ID or get dropped if the prior call was a notification. The author provides a functional test demonstrating that invalid batch elements duplicate prior IDs and drop notification errors on master, both of which are resolved.

risk.why: A mistake in JSON-RPC request parsing could corrupt batch responses or cause unintended response dropping for RPC clients.
